content: Lentinan, derived from Lentinus edodes (shiitake mushroom), is administered at a dose of 1 to 4 mg intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) once per week. It is indicated for use in cancer and HIV treatment. Evidence suggests it may be potentially effective as an adjunct therapy when combined with didanosine in HIV management. However, there is insufficient evidence to definitively rate its efficacy as an adjunctive treatment for breast, gastric, or prostate cancers. Preliminary findings indicate possible improvement in these conditions, but no conclusive results have been established. Adverse effects associated with lentinan include thrombocytopenia. Chronic consumption of large doses of whole shiitake mushrooms has been linked to dermatitis and eosinophilia. Hypersensitivity reactions have also been reported. Regarding pregnancy, lentinan falls under Category A, meaning it is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk. However, specific data on its safety during lactation is not available. Cost information and comprehensive interaction data are not provided in this context.
